inline.s: Maitreya Bodhisattva said to the Buddha: In this Saha world, and in the many Buddha-lands, how numerous are the irreversible bodhisattvas who will be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss? The Buddha told Maitreya Bodhisattva: In this Saha world there are seventy-two billion irreversible bodhisattvas, who have already made offerings to countless Buddhas and planted the roots of every virtue; they will be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. As for the lesser bodhisattvas who cultivate merit, the number of those who will be reborn there is beyond reckoning.

(The Saha world) The word 'Saha' originally referred to the southern continent Jambudvipa where we dwell; in later times it came to designate the three-thousand-great-thousand world system taught by Shakyamuni Buddha, the hundred billion Sumeru worlds being collectively called Saha, with the World-Honored One as the original teacher of this Saha world. In this passage, 'this Saha world' refers to the three-thousand-great-thousand world system that Shakyamuni Buddha teaches. (Lesser bodhisattvas) Bodhisattvas who have not yet reached the stage of irreversibility.

[Not only the bodhisattvas of my land who are reborn in that land Ã¢â‚¬â€ in the other Buddha-lands as well it is the same. From the Buddha-land of Far-Reaching Light, eighteen kotis of bodhisattva mahasattvas are born in that land. In the northeast, from the Buddha-land of the Treasury of Jewels, nine billion(?) irreversible bodhisattvas will be reborn there. From the Buddha-lands of Measureless Sound, Radiance, Dragon-Devas, Supreme Power, Lion, Free from Dust, Leader of Virtue, Benevolent King, and Flower Banner, the irreversible bodhisattvas who will be reborn there number anywhere from tens of billions to hundreds of billions, even to tens of trillions(?).]

Not only the bodhisattvas of my Buddha-land are reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss; in the other Buddha-lands as well it is the same. From the Buddha-land of Far-Reaching Light, eighteen kotis of great bodhisattvas are reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. In the northeast, from the Buddha-land of the Treasury of Jewels, nine billion irreversible bodhisattvas will be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. From the Buddha-lands of Measureless Sound, Radiance, Dragon-Devas, Supreme Power, Lion, Free from Dust, Leader of Virtue, Benevolent King, and Flower Banner, the irreversible bodhisattvas who will be reborn there number anywhere from tens of billions to hundreds of billions, even to tens of trillions.
The above briefly names the eleven Buddha-lands of other directions and the number of bodhisattvas who will be reborn there.

[The twelfth Buddha is named Unsurpassable Flower. He has countless hosts of bodhisattvas, all irreversible, wise and valiant, who have already made offerings to measureless Buddhas, endowed with great vigor, advancing toward the One Vehicle. Within seven days they are able to grasp the firm Dharma practiced by the great beings over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas. These bodhisattvas shall all be reborn there.]

The twelfth Buddha is named Unsurpassable Flower. He has countless hosts of bodhisattvas, all in the stage of irreversibility Ã¢â‚¬â€ wise and valiant, who have already made offerings to measureless Buddhas, endowed with great vigor, and who have vowed to advance to the One Vehicle (ultimate Buddhahood). Within seven days they are able to grasp the firm Dharma practiced by the great beings over hundreds of thousands of millions of kalpas. Such bodhisattvas shall all be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

[The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearlessness. He has a host of seventy-nine billion great bodhisattvas, and the lesser bodhisattvas and bhikshus, beyond all counting, shall all be reborn there. The names of the Buddhas of the ten directions and of the host of bodhisattvas who will be reborn there Ã¢â‚¬â€ even were one to speak only their names, they would never be exhausted throughout a kalpa.]

The thirteenth Buddha is named Fearlessness, and He has a host of seventy-nine billion great bodhisattvas, together with measureless lesser bodhisattvas and a host of bhikshus, all of whom shall be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. As for the names of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the host of bodhisattvas who will be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss Ã¢â‚¬â€ even were one to speak only their names, they could never be exhausted throughout a kalpa.

[The Buddha told Maitreya: Behold those bodhisattva mahasattvas who have well attained the benefit. If there is a good man or good woman who, having heard the name of Amitabha Buddha, can give rise to a single thought of loving joy, take refuge and bow with veneration,
and practice as it is taught,

know that this person has gained great benefit and shall obtain the merit spoken of above. His mind is neither lowly nor proud; he perfects wholesome roots, all of which grow ever higher. Know that this person is not of the Lesser Vehicle Ã¢â‚¬â€ in my Dharma he is called the foremost disciple.]

The Buddha told Maitreya Bodhisattva: Behold those great bodhisattvas who have been reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss Ã¢â‚¬â€ they have well attained the benefit. If there is a good man or good woman who, having heard the name of Amitabha Buddha, can give rise to a single thought of loving joy, take refuge and bow with veneration, and practice as it is taught, know that this person has gained great benefit and shall obtain the merit spoken of above. His mind is neither lowly nor proud; he perfects wholesome roots, all of which grow ever higher. Know that this person is not of the Lesser Vehicle Ã¢â‚¬â€ in my Dharma he is called the foremost disciple.

(Well attained the benefit) Those born in the highest grade, upon seeing the Buddha and hearing the Dharma, realize the Unborn and ascend to the eighth ground. Hence it is said they 'well attain the benefit.'
The Sutra of the Contemplation on the Buddha of Measureless Life says:

'At the time of his birth in that land, because this person is vigorous and valiant, Amitabha Tathagata, together with Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, countless transformation Buddhas, hundreds of thousands of millions of bhikshus and the assembly of shravakas, measureless devas, and palaces of seven jewels Ã¢â‚¬â€ Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva holds the adamantine throne and comes with Mahasthamaprapta Bodhisattva before the practitioner. Amitabha Buddha releases a great light that illuminates the practitioner's body, and with all the bodhisattvas reaches out a hand to welcome him. Avalokiteshvara and Mahasthamaprapta, with countless bodhisattvas, praise the practitioner and encourage his mind. The practitioner, seeing all this, rejoices with leaping delight; he sees his own body seated upon the adamantine throne, following behind the Buddha, and in the twinkling of an eye is born in that land. Once born there, he sees the Buddha's body complete in every mark, sees the bodhisattvas complete in every mark, and hears the wonderful Dharma proclaimed by the radiant jewel trees. Having heard it,
he realizes the patience of the Unborn Dharma,

and in an instant goes to serve all the Buddhas throughout the ten directions, receiving prophecy in turn before each Buddha. Returning to his own land, he gains measureless hundreds of thousands of dharani gates. This is called the birth of the highest grade.'

(The eighth ground) The eighth of the bodhisattva's ten grounds is called the Immovable Ground. On this ground the bodhisattva abides in the patience of the Unborn, cuts off all exertion, body and mind made still as empty space; he fulfills the paramita of vows, and with a mind of nirvana remains serene and unmoving Ã¢â‚¬â€ hence it is called the Immovable Ground. (The ten grounds) In the bodhisattva's practice of the fifty-two stages, the fifth group of ten positions is called the ten grounds. On these ten grounds one gradually opens the Buddha-realm and attains the wisdom of all modes; since this already belongs to the holy stage, it is also called the ten sages.

[Therefore I say to you who dwell among gods, humans, and asuras: you should love and delight in the practice, giving rise to a mind of reverence and wonder. In this sutra take it as your guide. If you wish to cause measureless beings to quickly and peacefully abide without falling back, and if you wish to see that vast and majestic, supremely adorned Buddha-land of complete merit, you should rouse diligence and listen to this Dharma-gate.]

Therefore I say to you who dwell among gods, humans, and asuras: you should love and delight in practicing the Pure Land Dharma-gate, giving rise to a mind of reverence and wonder. In this sutra take it as your guide. If you wish to cause measureless beings to quickly and peacefully abide without falling back, and if you wish to make those who long to see that vast and majestic, supremely adorned Buddha-land of complete merit be reborn there, you should rouse diligence and listen to this Pure Land Dharma-gate.
(In this sutra take it as your guide) Being instructed by this sutra, one gives rise to true faith and practices as it is taught.

[For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a mind of retreat, flattery, or deceit. Even were one to enter a great fire, he should not doubt or regret. Why is that? Because those measureless millions of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle Dharma-gate, honoring and listening to it without turning away. Many bodhisattvas desire to hear this sutra yet cannot. Therefore you should seek this Dharma.]

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, do not give rise to a mind of retreat, flattery, or deceit. Even were one to enter a great fire, he should not doubt or regret. Why is that? Because those measureless millions of bodhisattvas all seek this subtle Pure Land Dharma-gate, honoring and listening to it without turning away. Many bodhisattvas desire to hear this sutra yet cannot. Therefore you should eagerly seek this Pure Land Dharma-gate.

blocks.text: Receiving the Prophecy of Bodhi, Chapter Forty-Four

inline.s: [If in a future age, even down to the time when the true Dharma is extinguished, there are beings who plant all manner of wholesome roots and have already made offerings to measureless Buddhas Ã¢â‚¬â€ by the power of the Tathagatas' blessing they are able to obtain this vast Dharma-gate, to grasp and uphold it, and shall obtain the vast wisdom of all modes. In that Dharma they attain vast understanding and great joy, proclaiming it widely to others and ever delighting in practice.]

If in a future age, even down to the time when the true Dharma is extinguished, there are beings who plant all manner of wholesome roots and have already made offerings to measureless Buddhas Ã¢â‚¬â€ because they are blessed by the awesome power of Amitabha Buddha, they are able to obtain this vast Dharma-gate (the Pure Land Dharma-gate), to grasp and uphold it, and shall obtain the vast wisdom of all modes. In that Dharma they attain vast understanding and great joy, proclaiming it widely to others and ever delighting in practice.

(The vast Dharma-gate) In the age of the Dharma's end, of countless millions who practice, rarely one attains the Way; only by relying on Buddha-recitation does one cross the sea of birth and death. Thus the Pure Land Dharma-gate is a gate that broadly delivers living beings, and so it is called the 'vast Dharma-gate.' (The wisdom of all modes) The wisdom within all wisdom, that is, the Buddha's wisdom.

[All good men and good women who, with regard to this Dharma, whether they have already sought it, now seek it, or will seek it, shall all gain the good benefit. You should abide in it without doubt, planting all manner of wholesome roots, and constantly practice so as to be free of doubt and obstruction, never entering the prison of all kinds of precious attainments.]

All good men and good women who, with regard to this Dharma, whether they have already sought it, now seek it, or will seek it, shall all gain the good benefit. You should abide unhesitatingly, planting all manner of wholesome roots, and constantly practice so that you are free of doubt and obstruction, never entering the prison of all kinds of wealth and attainments.

[Ajita, beings of such great majestic virtue are able to give rise to the vast and special gate of the Buddha-Dharma. Because this Dharma has not been heard, one hundred million bodhisattvas have retreated from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.]

Maitreya, beings of such great majestic virtue (those who, with regard to this Dharma, whether they have already sought it, now seek it, or will seek it) are able to give rise to faith in the vast and supremely skillful gate of the Buddha-Dharma. Because this Dharma-gate has not been heard, one hundred million bodhisattvas have retreated from anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
(The supremely skillful Dharma-gate) The Pure Land Dharma-gate is the expedient of expedients, the shortcut among shortcuts; hence it is the supremely skillful Dharma-gate.

[If there are beings who, with regard to this sutra, copy and make offerings to it, uphold, receive, and recite it, and in an instant proclaim it for others, urging them to listen, without giving rise to worry or distress Ã¢â‚¬â€ nay, who ponder day and night that Buddha-land and the Buddha's merit Ã¢â‚¬â€ they shall never retreat from the supreme Way.]

If there are beings who, with regard to this sutra, copy and make offerings to it, uphold, receive, and recite it, and in an instant proclaim it for others, urging them to listen, without giving rise to worry or distress Ã¢â‚¬â€ nay, who ponder day and night the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss and the merit of Amitabha Buddha Ã¢â‚¬â€ they shall never retreat from the supreme Way, the Way of Buddhahood.

[At the moment of death, even were the three-thousand-great-thousand world filled with a great fire, he is able to pass beyond it and be born in that land. Such a person has already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi. All Tathagatas alike praise him. Therefore you should single-mindedly believe and receive, holding, reciting, proclaiming, and practicing.]

At the moment of their death, even were the three-thousand-great-thousand world filled with a great fire, they are able to pass beyond it and be born in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Such persons have already met the Buddhas of the past and received the prophecy of bodhi (the prophecy that they shall certainly become Buddhas in the future). All Tathagatas alike praise them. Therefore you should single-mindedly believe and receive this sutra, holding, reciting, proclaiming, and practicing it.

blocks.text: That This Sutra Alone Is Left Behind, Chapter Forty-Five

inline.s: [I now speak this sutra and Dharma for all beings, causing them to see Amitabha Buddha and all that is in his land. Whatever is to be done, they may all seek it. Do not, after my passing, give rise to doubt again.]

I now speak this sutra and Dharma for all beings, causing them to see Amitabha Buddha and all that is in his land. Whatever is to be done (that is, the faith, vow, and practice of seeking rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss), strive to accomplish it. Do not, after my passing, give rise to doubt again.

[In a future age, when the sutras and the Way are extinguished, I, out of compassion and sorrow, will leave this sutra alone, to remain for a hundred years. Whatever beings encounter this sutra, according to their aspirations, shall all be delivered.]

In a future age, when the sutras and the Way are extinguished, I, out of compassion and sorrow, will leave this sutra alone, to remain for another hundred years. Whatever beings encounter this sutra, according to their aspirations, shall all be delivered.
(When the sutras and the Way are extinguished) The Commentary on the Illustrations of the Pure Land says:

'When in a future age the sutras and the Way are extinguished Ã¢â‚¬â€ this points to the matter of the Dharma's total extinction in the future. Shakyamuni's right Dharma lasts five hundred years, the Semblance Dharma a thousand years, and the Debased Dharma ten thousand years. When all these are past, it is called extinction.'
Master Shandao, in his Praise of Rebirth, says:
'At the end of the ten thousand years the Triple Gem is extinguished, yet this sutra remains for a hundred years.'

(The right Dharma, Semblance Dharma, and Debased Dharma) The Buddha-Dharma is divided into three periods: the period of right Dharma, the period of Semblance Dharma, and the period of the Debased Dharma. In the period of right Dharma, though the Buddha has passed away, the Dharma appears in its true form; there is teaching, there is practice, and there are those who realize the fruit Ã¢â‚¬â€ this is called the period of right Dharma. In the period of Semblance Dharma, 'semblance' means similar; it resembles the right Dharma yet is not the right Dharma. In this period there is teaching and there is practice, but those who realize the fruit are already few. In the period of the Debased Dharma, 'debased' means fading; this period turns toward the dregs, with only the teaching and no practice, and no one at all who realizes the fruit.

[The Tathagata's arising in the world is hard to meet, hard to see. The sutras and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain, hard to hear. To encounter a good spiritual friend, hear the Dharma, and be able to practice it is also difficult. If one hears this sutra and, with faith and joy, receives and upholds it Ã¢â‚¬â€ this is the hardest of all difficulties; there is none harder than this.]

The Tathagata's arising in the world is hard to meet, hard to see. The sutras and the Way of the Buddhas are hard to obtain, hard to hear. To encounter a good spiritual friend, hear the Dharma, and be able to practice it is also difficult. If one hears this sutra and, with faith and joy, receives and upholds it Ã¢â‚¬â€ this is the hardest of all difficulties; there is none harder than this.

[If there are beings who, having heard the name of the Buddha, are pure and clear of heart, leap with joy, their hair standing on end, or who shed tears Ã¢â‚¬â€ these have all, in former lives, practiced the Buddha-Way, and so are no ordinary people.]

If there are beings who, having heard the name of Amitabha Buddha, are pure and clear of heart, leap with joy, their hair standing on end, or who shed tears Ã¢â‚¬â€ these have all, in former lives, practiced the Buddha-Way, and so are no ordinary people.
(Having heard the name of the Buddha) Having heard the name of Amitabha Buddha.
The Sutra of the Buddha of Measureless Life, spoken by the Buddha (the Wei translation), reads
'having heard the name of that Buddha'
, the Assembled Tathagata of Measureless Life (the Tang translation) reads
'hearing the name of that Buddha'
, and the Great Vehicle Sutra of Infinite Life and Adornment, spoken by the Buddha (the Song translation), reads
'having heard the name of the Buddha of Measureless Life'

[If one hears the Buddha's name yet harbors doubt in his heart, believing not at all in the words of the Buddha's sutras Ã¢â‚¬â€ such a one has come from the evil paths; his past karmic obstacles are not yet exhausted, and he is not yet meant to be delivered. Hence his heart doubts, and he does not believe or turn toward it.]

If one hears the name of Amitabha Buddha yet harbors doubt in his heart, believing not at all in the words of the Buddha's sutras Ã¢â‚¬â€ such a one has come from the evil paths; his past karmic obstacles are not yet exhausted, and he is not yet meant to be delivered. Hence his heart doubts, and he cannot believe or accept it.
